title: Basin hopping from the best
spec: After about 40% of the time, switch to perturbation search. Take the best (c,r), add Gaussian noise (sd about 0.03) to the centres, set radii to 0.8 of their values, re-run SLSQP, and accept if better. Repeat until the time is used.

title: Perturb phase: 25 percent restart, chained acceptance
spec: Set the restart phase to 25% of the time. Afterwards keep a current packing and a best packing. Each cycle perturbs the current one (radii x0.5, centre noise sd chosen from [0.01,0.02,0.04]), re-optimises with SLSQP, and accepts it as current if its sum is >= current sum - 0.002 (otherwise stays). Track best separately and return best.

title: Perturb-and-accept chain from current packing
spec: After 25% of the time, keep a current packing cur (initially best). Each iteration: perturb cur with centre noise sd drawn from [0.01,0.02,0.03], radii x0.5, re-optimise with SLSQP, repair. Accept as the new cur if its sum is >= cur.sum - 0.002 (small tolerance); update best separately. Reset cur to best if no best improvement for 8 iterations.

title: Soft-start with a radius cap
spec: First solve with a constraint r<=0.12 and the same sum objective, then release the cap and continue from that result. This regularises the early phase and avoids a few huge circles.

title: Penalty-free log-barrier warm start
spec: For each fresh random restart, before SLSQP, run a few L-BFGS-B iterations minimising -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2) + wall penalties over (centres, radii) with mu increasing 10, 100, 1000 across three stages of 30 iterations each, using an analytic gradient via numpy. Then hand the result to SLSQP with MAX_ITER 150. Keeps the existing perturbation phase unchanged.

title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000
spec: Set MAX_ITER=1000 and add ftol=1e-12 to the SLSQP options so that each run converges fully. Combine with analytic Jacobians if possible. Fewer but fully converged runs usually give better local optima than truncated ones.

title: Adaptive restart/perturb split by success rate
spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch with a bandit: each iteration chooses between a fresh restart and a perturbation of the best, with probability proportional to the (smoothed) count of past improvements per method, starting at 50/50 with prior 1 success each, with perturbation forced at least 50% after 20% of time.

title: Short-iteration restart sweep
spec: In the restart phase, use MAX_ITER=80 for the first 15% of the time. Keep the best 3 packings. Then run a 300-iteration SLSQP continuation from each. After that, perturb the best as in slot 2 for the remaining time.

title: Two-stage: fast screen, then polish
spec: Run many short SLSQP runs (maxiter 60). Keep the top 3 by sum of radii after repair. Then continue each with maxiter 500 and ftol 1e-13 starting from the result. Return the best.

title: Radius-weight annealed objective
spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP first with objective -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i = 1 + 0.5*u_i, u_i uniform in [-1,1] per circle, for 50 iterations, then switch to the true objective for the full MAX_ITER. Weights are drawn from rng. This breaks symmetry between circles and encourages varied radius distributions.

title: Hex-defect starts with 26 circles
spec: For half of the fresh restarts, build the start from a hexagonal arrangement. Use 5 rows alternating 5 and 6 circles, which gives 27 positions, and drop one random circle. Use spacing about 0.18 with an offset on alternate rows. Add gaussian noise sd 0.02 to the centres, set the radii to 0.08, and clip the centres to [0.05,0.95]. The other half stay uniform random.

title: Weighted-objective warm start
spec: For each fresh start, first run 50 SLSQP iterations maximising sum of w_i*r_i with random weights w_i uniform in [0.5,1.5], then continue with the true objective for up to 200 iterations from that result. The random weights bias which circles grow large, diversifying basins.

title: Block rotation perturbation
spec: In the perturbation phase, half the time pick a random centre point and a radius of 0.25-0.4. Rotate the circles inside that disc about the point by a random angle of 20-90 degrees. Set radii x0.5 and re-optimise from the result. Otherwise use the existing jitter.

title: Active-pair constraint pruning
spec: Include only constraints for pairs with distance less than 0.45 at the start of each SLSQP run, and re-check validity after. Solve again with all pairs if violated. This reduces the cost per iteration (325 pairs down to about 100).

title: Weighted objective warm start
spec: For fresh random starts, first run 50 SLSQP iterations with the objective -sum(w_i r_i). Draw w_i from uniform(0.5, 1.5) per restart. Then run the normal 200-iteration SLSQP on the true objective from that point. This diversifies the basins reached.

title: Bounded SLSQP with box bounds
spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5], and remove the radius>=0 constraint r from cons (keep the wall constraints). This shrinks the constraint vector and keeps the iterates in a sane region. Change nothing else.

title: Short-iteration restarts for the first phase
spec: Set MAX_ITER to 100 for fresh random starts in the first 30% of the time, which gives about twice as many restarts. Re-run the best 2 of those with 400 iterations from their own end points. Then proceed with the perturbation phase from the best. Differs from earlier screening ideas because there is no threshold and no separate screen period.

title: Bounded-variable SLSQP with box bounds
spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Remove the explicit r>=0 constraint block from cons. This shrinks the constraint vector by 26 entries and keeps iterates in range, so restarts may converge better. Leave everything else unchanged.

title: Larger iteration budget with fewer restarts
spec: Raise MAX_ITER to 600 for both fresh and perturbed solves, and also pass options ftol=1e-10 to SLSQP. Fresh starts are fewer but fully converged; keep the 30% restart / perturb split from slot 2. This tests whether under-converged runs are the bottleneck.

title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation
spec: In the perturbation phase, half the time scale the best packing's centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor from uniform(0.85,0.95), radii x0.5, add noise sd 0.01, and re-optimise with SLSQP. This compresses the packing toward the centre so that the optimiser re-forms the wall contacts and finds different contact graphs. The other half uses the existing jitter.

title: Radius-weight annealed objective
spec: In _solve_once for fresh starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) minimises -sum(w*r) with w=1+0.5*(r_init-rank-based random values drawn from U(-1,1)) fixed per circle. Stage 2 (200 iterations) uses the plain objective starting from the stage 1 result. Apply it to half of the fresh restarts only.

title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation
spec: In the perturbation phase, with probability 0.5 build the start from the best packing by scaling all centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor drawn from U(0.85,0.95), halving the radii and adding noise sd 0.01 to the centres. Otherwise use the existing perturbation. Re-optimise with SLSQP as before.

title: Two-radius-class starts
spec: For fresh random starts, assign 4 to 6 circles an initial radius of 0.13 and the others 0.07 (random which), placing centres by sequential dart throwing with rejection so initial overlaps are small (up to 200 tries each, largest first). This mimics the known big/small structure of the best packings.

title: Trust-constr free final polish
spec: After the main loop ends (stop it at 90% of TIME_FRACTION), take the best packing and run scipy trust-constr (or SLSQP with ftol=1e-15, maxiter 300) from it with the same constraints, accept only if the repaired sum improves. Repair afterwards as before. Use remaining time only; skip if less than 1.5 s remain.

title: Elite recombination by region
spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings from the restart phase. In the perturbation phase, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut at a position in 0.3-0.7. Take the circles of parent A with centres on one side and the circles of parent B on the other side. Fill to n circles by dropping the smallest extras or adding circles at random positions with small radii. Then run SLSQP from the child with radii x0.5. Fall back to perturbation of the best if the child is worse than the best.

title: Drop one circle and re-grow with 25-circle solutions
spec: For the first 20% of the time, solve n-1=25 circles with random restarts. Then for each of the top 3 solutions, insert a 26th circle at the largest empty hole (the point maximising the distance to the circles and the walls, found on a 50x50 grid), set its radius to 0.03 and the other radii x0.9, and run full SLSQP. Use the best result as the incumbent, and go on with the existing perturbation phase for the rest of the time.

title: Corner-pair anchored starts
spec: For fresh random starts, put 4 circles with initial radius 0.12 near the four corners (centres at 0.12 from both walls plus noise sd 0.01). Place the remaining 22 uniformly in [0.1,0.9] with initial radius 0.05. Run the normal SLSQP. Use this for half the fresh restarts and keep the rest as is.

title: Elite crossover by region
spec: Keep the top 4 distinct packings from the restart phase. In the later phase, build a child by choosing a random vertical or horizontal cut line, taking the circles of parent A on one side, and of parent B on the other, adjusting to exactly 26 circles by deleting the smallest or adding random points. Radii x0.5, SLSQP, repair; insert into the pool if good.

title: Keep an elite pool and recombine
spec: Keep the top 5 solutions. To create a new start, take the left half (x<0.5) circles from one elite and the right half from another, fill to 26 circles by adding or removing random ones, then optimise.

title: Perturbation by random-rotation of a row/block
spec: In the second phase, perturb the best packing by a structured move: pick a random vertical or horizontal strip of width 0.3, shift the centres of the circles in it by a random offset of up to 0.08 along the strip's length (wrapping with clipping to [0.05,0.95]), set radii x0.5, re-optimise, repair, and keep if better. This explores collective moves that independent jitter cannot.

title: Smooth penalty objective with growing radii (inflation schedule)
spec: For fresh random starts, replace the SLSQP start by an inflation scheme: all radii equal to a common scale s, centres optimised by L-BFGS-B on the sum of squared overlaps plus wall violations, with s raised in 6 steps from 0.06 to 0.11 (warm start each step). Then use the resulting centres with radii 0.9 of the feasible values as the SLSQP start. Use the seed rng for the initial centres.

title: Trust-constr final polish
spec: After the main loop (stop it at 85% of the time limit), take the best packing and run scipy minimize with method='trust-constr' on the same objective and constraints (variables bounded to [0,1] for centres and [0,0.5] for radii), maxiter 300, starting from the best. Keep the result only if after _repair its sum of radii exceeds the best. Keep the existing repair step.

title: Two-radius-class starts
spec: For fresh random starts, choose k uniformly from 4..8 large circles with initial radius 0.14 and the rest with initial radius 0.07. Place the large circles by rejection sampling at least 0.25 apart, the small ones uniformly in [0.05,0.95]. Run the normal SLSQP. Use this for all fresh starts.

title: Variable-radius-weight objective annealing
spec: In _solve_once for fresh starts, first solve with objective -sum(r_i^p) with p=0.5 (favours equalising radii) for 60 iterations, then continue with the true objective -sum(r) for 200 iterations starting from that solution. Use the same constraints. Different from random per-circle weights: it is a deterministic concave power transform.

title: Tune restart fraction and iteration cap together
spec: Set the switch from fresh restarts to perturbation at 15% of the time limit instead of 30%, and use MAX_ITER=120 for perturbation solves (which start near an optimum) while keeping 200 for fresh starts. This yields more perturbation cycles from a good basin.

title: Drop-one and regrow from 25-circle solution
spec: Take the best packing, delete a random circle (preferring the smallest 5), and re-solve SLSQP with n=25 for 100 iterations. Then insert a new circle with a small initial radius 0.02 at the point of greatest clearance, found over a 100x100 grid as the distance to nearest circle edge and walls. Re-optimise all 26 with SLSQP for 200 iterations. Run this in the perturbation phase half the time, in place of the x0.5 perturbation.

title: Boundary-ring plus interior structured starts
spec: Half of fresh restarts: put k random between 14 and 18 circles evenly spaced on a ring inset 0.08 from the square boundary (with a random angular offset and small noise sd 0.01), and put the remaining circles at random positions in [0.25,0.75]^2. Initial radius 0.06 for the ring and 0.08 for the interior. The other half stay uniform random.

title: Remove 3 smallest and reinsert, 100% of perturbations plus sd jitter
spec: In the perturbation phase, take the best packing, remove the 3 smallest circles, and place them at random points drawn from the 10 largest-clearance candidates among 2000 random samples (clearance = distance to nearest remaining centre minus its radius, and distance to walls). Give them radius 0.03, jitter all centres with sd 0.01, scale radii x0.5, and re-optimise with SLSQP. Alternate with the slot-2 perturbation 50/50. It differs from slot 29 in using the top-10 candidates and the extra jitter.

title: Tight-SLSQP polish with active-set constraint set
spec: After the restart/perturb loop ends at 85% of time, take the best packing and run one SLSQP using only pair constraints whose distance minus radii sum is below 0.02 (plus all wall constraints), with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 500, starting from the packing with radii unchanged. Accept only if the repaired result has a larger sum. Reserve 10% of the time limit for this.

title: Drop-one regrow from 27 circles
spec: Spend 15% of the time solving 27-circle problems with random starts (n+1 circles). Then for the best 27 packing, delete each of the 27 circles in turn, giving 26-circle starts, re-optimise each with SLSQP (radii x0.9), and keep the best. After that, use the normal slot-2 perturbation of the best until the time runs out. The rest of the time uses the usual restarts.

title: Squeeze-and-expand wall perturbation
spec: In the perturbation phase, scale the best packing's centres about (0.5,0.5) by a factor from uniform(0.85,0.95), set radii to 0.5 times the original, add noise sd 0.01, and re-optimise with SLSQP. This creates compressed structures that relax into different arrangements, as a replacement for pure Gaussian jitter in half of the cycles.

title: Soft-min radius-weight annealing
spec: For fresh random starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) uses the objective -sum(w_i*r_i) with w_i = 1 + 0.5*(r_i_start-mean) style fixed random weights drawn from U(0.5,1.5) per circle. Stage 2 (200 iterations) uses the true objective starting from the stage-1 solution. Time stays shared with the usual loop and only 50% of fresh starts use this.

title: Tabu perturbation: re-optimise from a different elite packing each round
spec: Keep a list of the top 8 packings from the restart phase, with their sums. In the perturbation phase, pick the parent by rank-weighted sampling (weights 1/rank), not always the best. Apply the radii x0.5 plus sd noise perturbation, re-optimise, and insert the child into the list if it beats the worst and is distinct (sum differs by more than 1e-6). This lets the search spread across several basins, unlike the earlier always-best perturbation.

title: Adaptive restart/perturb split
spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch with an adaptive rule. Alternate between a fresh random restart and a perturbation of the best packing. Track the number of improvements from each type, and choose the next type with probability proportional to (successes+1)/(trials+2). Allow perturbations only after 10% of the time has elapsed.

title: Restart phase 20% with larger perturbation pool
spec: Set the restart phase to 20% of the time. In the perturbation phase, choose sd from [0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08] and radii scale from [0.3, 0.5, 0.7] at random each time. Perturb the best packing only.

title: Radius-weight annealed objective
spec: For fresh starts, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 (60 iterations) maximises sum(r_i^0.5) which favours equal radii. Stage 2 (200 iterations) maximises sum(r). Use the same constraints. Take the stage 1 result as the start for stage 2 without shrinking radii.

title: Repulsion-energy initialisation (Riesz) with size gradient
spec: For fresh starts, draw 26 random points and relax them with 100 steps of gradient descent on the energy sum 1/d^2 over pairs plus wall repulsion 1/(2*wall distance)^2. Use a small random multiplicative jitter of 5%. Set the initial radii to 0.4 times the nearest-neighbour distance, capped by wall distance. Then run SLSQP as usual. This gives evenly spread starts that differ from the Lloyd, hex and grid starts tried so far, because they come from a physical relaxation.

title: Final tight polish with bounded SLSQP
spec: After the main loop, run SLSQP on the best packing once more starting from its exact centres and radii (not shrunk), with maxiter=500, ftol=1e-12, and bounds on variables (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]). Then repair, and keep the result only if the sum is larger than the current best.

title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts
spec: For fresh random restarts, draw 26 uniform points in the unit square, then run 8 Lloyd iterations using a 40x40 grid of sample points: assign each sample to its nearest point and move each point to the mean of its samples. Use the result as the initial centres, with radius 0.05. Keep the perturbation phase unchanged.

title: Batch-parallel-style population of perturbations
spec: After 30% of time, generate a batch of 4 perturbed children of the best (different sd), run each with MAX_ITER 60 only, then fully optimise (300 iterations) only the child with the highest intermediate sum. Repeat. This is a successive-halving selection inside the perturbation phase.

title: Lloyd-relaxed centroidal starts
spec: For fresh random starts, draw 26 uniform points, then run 10 Lloyd iterations on a 60x60 grid of sample points in the unit square (assign each sample to its nearest point, move each point to the centroid of its samples). Use the result as the centres with initial radius 0.06 and run SLSQP as before.

title: Two-radius-class starts
spec: For fresh random starts, choose k uniformly from 4..8 circles as large with initial radius 0.14 and the other circles with initial radius 0.07, centres uniform in [0.1,0.9]. The best known packings have a mix of large and small circles, so this gives a start closer to that structure.

title: Chained perturbation with acceptance
spec: In the perturbation phase, keep a current packing separate from the best. Each step perturbs the current packing (jitter sd 0.01-0.03, radii x0.5), re-optimises, and accepts it if its sum is >= current - 0.003. Otherwise revert to the current packing. Reset the current packing to the best every 8 failures. Update the best whenever the sum improves.

title: Adaptive restart-vs-perturb split by success
spec: Replace the fixed 30% switch. Start with restarts only. After 15% of the time, run perturbation rounds, tracking the number of improvements from perturbation. If no perturbation improved the best in the last 8 attempts, do one fresh restart. Always run perturbation in the last 40% of the time.

title: Objective smoothing via radius-weight annealing
spec: Run SLSQP first with objective -sum(w_i r_i) where w_i are random weights uniform(0.7,1.3) for 80 iterations, then continue with the true objective for 200 iterations. Applies to fresh random restarts only.

title: Larger count then prune: 28 circles to 26
spec: Spend 15% of the time optimising 28 circles. Then remove the 2 circles with the smallest radii, re-optimise the 26 that remain with SLSQP, and keep the best. Afterwards, the existing perturbation phase works on this best packing. The extra circles move the structure into denser arrangements.

title: Perturbation by radius-ordered inflation of the smallest circles
spec: In the perturbation phase, instead of scaling all radii by 0.5, take the best packing, set the 5 smallest circles' radii to 0 and all other radii to 0.9 times their value, and add centre noise sd 0.01. Then run SLSQP. The small circles can regrow wherever there is room, and the larger ones keep their structure. Use this in half of the perturbation steps.

title: Final best-of-all polishing with random small-sd restarts
spec: For the last 20% of the time, run only small perturbations of the best packing (centre sd 0.002 to 0.008, radii x0.95) and run SLSQP at MAX_ITER=100, accepting the child if its repaired sum improves. This is a fine local search around the best optimum. Keep the first 80% unchanged: 30% fresh restarts, then the perturbation phase.

title: Slack-free exact repair via scaling
spec: Replace the greedy pair-shrink _repair loop. Compute r = min(r, wall distance), then repeatedly scale r_i, r_j for the worst overlapping pair down with the existing code, but afterwards take a final pass that computes the largest radius for each circle in turn (r_i = min(wall dist, min_j(d_ij - r_j)) - 1e-12) in order of increasing radius, so that no valid slack is lost. Set SHRINK to 1e-12. Check that the result is still valid under the tolerance of 1e-10.

title: Adaptive annealed perturbation size with stagnation restarts
spec: In the perturbation phase, use sd that starts at 0.05 and is multiplied by 0.8 on each failure to improve the best, reset to 0.05 after sd drops below 0.004. If 15 consecutive failures occur, discard the best-so-far for perturbation purposes and run one fresh random restart as the new perturbation base (still keep the global best for return).
